A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a computational model of a CDR that is based on a SNN with an architecture that is inspired from the brain of a rat (Asada et. al. 2009; Xu et al, 2014) and that is capable to learn and to execute a task in an unknown environment.
we have developed a novel computational model of a CDR based on the combination of a SNN and an environment model (EM), and we have demonstrated its effectiveness for the development of a CDR.
we have developed a novel approach that allows the design of a SNN controller for the CDR system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we propose a novel computational model of CDR system based on the combination of computational systems biology and computational neuroscience approaches.

we can design a computational model of CDR system by using a computational systems biology approach that is based on the concept of a dynamical response of a SNN with an architecture that is inspired from biological neural systems.
we have proposed and tested a new method for developing CDR systems that can be used for the future generation robots with more intelligent cognitive abilities.
